drafts.title: Has Anyone Else Seen Newer Small LLMs Sacrifice World Knowledge for Coding Skills?
drafts.body: A 2025 Reddit post reports that newer small LLMs like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 show noticeably better coding and problem-solving performance compared to older models, yet their world knowledge is often worse—even compared to some older, lower-benchmarking models of similar size. For example, Qwen 3 8B reportedly underperforms Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma 2 9B on knowledge tests, while Qwen 3 14B fares worse than Phi 4 and Gemma 3 12B. The author suspects this trade-off stems from training data containing more problem-solving content but less knowledge-dense material. Given these observations rely on private test questions and specific models, has anyone else noticed this apparent tension between knowledge depth and problem-solving in recent smaller LLMs? How do you approach selecting models when you need both reliable factual knowledge and strong coding abilities locally?

drafts.title: Trade-off Between World Knowledge and Problem-Solving in Newer Small LLMs—Thoughts?
drafts.body: According to a 2025 user report, newer smaller LLMs such as Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 excel in coding and engineering problem solving compared to older models but show degraded world knowledge. The author’s private tests indicate models like Qwen 3 8B and 14B have poorer factual recall than older models like Llama 3.1 8B or Gemma 3 12B. Interestingly, some models like Llama 4 Maverick buck this trend by having strong knowledge but weaker problem-solving skills. The hypothesis is that training data for newer models emphasizes problem-solving tasks at the expense of knowledge-rich content. For those working locally with these models, how do you evaluate or balance these trade-offs in practice? Have you found any testing approaches or model choices that help maintain both knowledge accuracy and problem-solving strength?

drafts.title: Balancing Knowledge and Problem-Solving in Small LLMs: Insights from a 2025 Report
drafts.body: A 2025 Reddit post highlights a curious pattern: newer small LLMs, while scoring higher on coding and problem-solving benchmarks, often show weaker world knowledge than older or similarly sized models. For instance, Granite 3.3 improved slightly on problem-solving compared to Granite 3.2 but declined in knowledge. Conversely, Llama 4 Maverick offers strong world knowledge but mediocre coding skills. The author speculates this trade-off arises because newer training data is richer in problem-solving content but less dense in factual knowledge. Given these findings are based on private test sets and specific models, does anyone have experience confirming this trade-off? What strategies do you use to assess or mitigate potential losses in knowledge while gaining problem-solving improvements?
